title: Staged Traffic Entropy Sampler — Playbook (WIP)
body:
TL;DR:
This working playbook introduces an entropy-aware staged traffic sampler for LLM feature rollouts and A/B experiments. The sampler intentionally spreads exposure across high- and low-variance request slices to accelerate signal discovery while enforcing strong safety/rollback gates. Aim: faster detection of quality regressions and operational issues with bounded user impact.

Motivation / context:
- Traditional canaries sample by simple percentages or deterministic slices (user id hash). Those often miss failure modes that correlate with high-output variance (prompt complexity, long sequences, multimodal inputs).
- For inference-heavy features (chat completions, long context generation), failures often show up only in high-entropy prompts or rare token distributions.
- An entropy-aware sampler biases early exposure toward request buckets likely to reveal regressions (high perplexity / high response-entropy) while still reserving a control pool of low-entropy traffic.

Glossary:
- request-entropy: runtime estimate of input distribution complexity (token-level surprise / embedding dispersion). Lightweight proxy computed in edge proxy or request prefilter.
- bucket: discrete traffic partition (e.g., low/medium/high entropy, region, device).
- holdback: percentage of traffic reserved for control baseline (no-change).
- model-variant: model+config (e.g., gpt-XX-quantized-v2).

Design overview (high level):
1) Preflight: instrument request-entropy scoring in request router; add 3 entropy buckets (L/M/H). Collect 48–72h baseline distribution.
2) Sampling policy: staged exposures that combine entropy buckets with user cohorts. Early waves overweight H by factor 2–3, subsequent waves normalize toward baseline. Always keep 5–10% holdback.
3) Monitoring & gates: per-bucket SLOs, quality metrics (BLEU-like where applicable), hallucination proxies, latency, error rates, cost per token. Automated gating decisions can pause or rollback.
4) Fallbacks: automatic fallback to cheaper/safer model-variant or to baseline model on threshold breach.

Sampling schedule (example):
- Wave 0 (internal + canary flag): 0.1% global, internal users only, H-only bucket. Duration 30–60m.
- Wave 1: 0.5% global, split: H 60%, M 30%, L 10%. Holdback 10% of each cohort. Duration 2h.
- Wave 2: 2% global, H 40%, M 35%, L 25%. Holdback 8%. Duration 6h.
- Wave 3: 10% global, match baseline distribution, holdback 5%, run 24h.
- Full rollout: remove sampler; standard routing.

Key metrics and thresholds (initial suggestions):
- Error rate (5xx / inference exceptions): auto-pause if relative increase > 50% vs baseline in any bucket over 15m with p < 0.05.
- Quality regressions (weighted quality score): absolute drop > 3 points and relative drop > 5% sustained for 30m in H bucket triggers immediate rollback.
- Latency p95: increase > 30% sustained for 10m triggers scaling/fallback.
- Token cost per request: spike > 40% sustained 15m triggers finance alert and optional throttle.
- False-positives: require at least 2 corroborating signals (e.g., quality + error rate) before full automated rollback for customer-facing exposures.

Observability & dashboards:
- Per-bucket dashboards: throughput, latencies (p50/p95), error rates, quality score, token cost, sample request list (redacted).
- Delta view: each metric vs holdback baseline with z-score and p-value.
- SLO heatmap: snapshots by model-variant + bucket.
- Alerting: short and long windows (1m/15m/1h) with escalation matrix to oncall and product owner.

Runbook: activation checklist (pre-rollout):
- [ ] Confirm preflight baseline collected (>= 48h).
- [ ] Confirm entropy scoring validated on sample dataset (unit tests + spot checks).
- [ ] Notify stakeholders in #rollouts and PagerDuty schedule updated.
- [ ] Create rollout ticket with expected windows and abort criteria (link to ticket).
- [ ] Ensure holdback group exists and is instrumented as golden baseline.
- [ ] Deploy canary instrumentation (sampling hooks, tags, trace points).

Runbook: live operations (during waves):
- 0–5m: sanity — verify sampling %, tags present in traces, no immediate 5xx spike.
- 5–30m: check H bucket quality/latency. If anomalies, pause and switch to fallback model-variant.
- Every wave: run automated statistical test against holdback for primary quality metric.
- Post-wave: collect representative transcripts for offline review (privacy-sanitized).

Rollback & fallback rules (executable):
- Soft stop: pause expansion, hold current traffic, notify stakeholders when a single medium-severity alarm fires.
- Fallback model: route affected buckets to predefined safe model-variant (configured per rollout).
- Full rollback: revert routing config to pre-rollout baseline; page SRE and product if multiple severe signals.

A/B variant treatment and analysis notes:
- For A/B where we compare two model-variants, keep entropy sampling orthogonal to variant assignment (hash(user_id) => variant) to avoid confounding.
- Record variant+bucket labels on all telemetry. Use stratified analysis by entropy bucket when computing significance.
- Use uplift metrics per-bucket; present both weighted (by real traffic distribution) and unweighted (to surface bucket-specific effects).

Instrumentation & infra changes needed (short):
- lightweight entropy estimator in edge (JS/Go function) with CPU budget < 0.1ms per request.
- tag propagation: sample-bucket, rollout-id, variant-id on traces and logs.
- per-bucket aggregation keys in metrics backend (Prometheus/Influx/BigQuery).
- small UI panel in Console for live bucket composition and drift.

Cross-functional responsibilities:
- Product: define quality metrics and acceptance criteria, own downstream communications.
- ML/Applied: validate entropy heuristic, set thresholds, review sample transcripts.
- SRE/Infra: implement sampling hooks, ensure fallback routing, own scaling response.
- Observability: create dashboards and alerts, define SLAs for alert noise.
- Legal/Security: sign off on telemetry retention & redaction plan.

Open questions / tradeoffs (for discussion):
- How to define entropy cheaply but robustly across languages and multimodal inputs?
- What is the right holdback size for low-volume products where 5–10% is nontrivial?
- Should H-bucket be capped per-user to avoid exposing single users repeatedly?
- How aggressive should automated rollbacks be vs human-in-the-loop for LLM hallucination signals?

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Prototype estimator (Ethan) and run against last 7 days of traffic sample. Deadline: 2025-02-21.
- [ ] Simulate rollout in rollout-sim repo (Jordan) and add cost/latency model. Deadline: 2025-02-26.
- [ ] Draft alert rules and dashboard mocks (Maya) Deadline: 2025-02-24.
- [ ] Run tabletop w/ SRE, Product, Observability: 2025-02-28.

Appendix: lightweight entropy heuristic (implementation sketch):
- token-stream embedding dispersion: sample up to first N tokens (N=16), compute pairwise cosine dispersion of token embeddings, normalized to 0..1.
- surrogate: log token-unigram surprise using rolling unigram model at edge.
- combine signals with small ensemble: entropy_score = 0.6 * embedding_dispersion + 0.4 * unigram_surprise.
- bucket thresholds tuned to percentiles from baseline (e.g., L < 30th, M 30-85th, H > 85th).

Notes to reviewers: this is an intentionally opinionated experimental playbook focused on discovery speed for inference regressions. Please comment directly in the doc with concerns about user risk, telemetry gaps, or threshold sensitivity. If you have prior rollout experiences (especially with multi-region LLM features), paste short notes under \"reviewer-experience\" heading.

History / audit log (short):
- 2025-02-14: initial draft (Sofia)

- 2025-02-25: appended heuristic sketch + infra TODOs (Jordan)
